key_insight: A dual-scale histopathology approach that combines 10x and 20x image analysis with late fusion improves automated detection of mycosis fungoides by capturing both tissue architecture and细胞-level detail.
clinical_relevance: This multimodal framework could support earlier screening of mycosis fungoides versus benign inflammatory skin disease and help stage confirmed cases using clinical metadata.
method: Dual-magnification CNNs trained on 10x and 20x histopathology images
Late-fusion ensemble to combine broad context with high-resolution cytological detail
Random forest model using 16 clinical features for MF staging
evidence_signal: On 6,267 images from 463 patients, the image-based model reached 83.58% accuracy and 89.13% sensitivity, while the clinical random forest achieved 96.6% accuracy and 93.8% sensitivity.
watch_item: Performance should be validated prospectively across external centers and workflows, since rare-disease imaging models can be sensitive to dataset and site differences.
paper_title: Detail in Context: A Dual-Scale Machine Learning Framework for Mycosis Fungoides Detection
